                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most capable immune system cell for killing tumor cells with decreased MHC class I expression is the natural killer (NK) cell. Normally, MHC class I molecules help display peptide fragments from within the cell to cytotoxic T-cells. When these molecules are downregulated, as observed in some tumor cells, it reduces the ability of cytotoxic T-cells to recognize and kill these cells. However, this decrease in MHC class I expression triggers an activation of NK cells, which are equipped to recognize and kill cells that have abnormally low levels of MHC class I. This mechanism is part of the immune system's innate response to cells that might evade the adaptive immune response. The evidence paths confirm the interaction between NK cells and cells with altered MHC class I expression, supporting their role in responding to and killing such tumor cells. Other immune cells like B-cells, macrophages, and eosinophils do not primarily target cells based on MHC class I expression levels and are thus less effective in this specific context.
